steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mix banana, oil, egg, and vanilla in a medium bowl.
Combine flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Stir in banana mixture until just blended. Fold in chocolate chips. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin tin, filling 3/4 full.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove muffins to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Chip Banana Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Chocolate chips and cocoa team well with banana in these lovely muffins that are made even more delicious with the addition of vanilla.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Chip Banana Muffins

review.reviewBody: This recipe is awesome. I did change some things: I used Whole Wheat flour (With the Cocoa color, you cant even tell, if youve got picky eaters), and I used half the oil . I made up the 1/3c difference with milk. I also added a handful of walnuts. This probably shouldnt be an every day breakfast, but its amazingly good!

Just made this for the first time! I used one large banana, substituted applesauce for the oil, and did half whole wheat flour. So amazing! I also used a six count oversized muffin tin and it took only 18 minutes to cook. This is definitely a favorite!!!

These are so moist and yummy! I used 1/4 white sugar and 1/4 cup brown sugar. I also used coconut oil since that’s what I had. I added a few extra chocolate chips on top before baking the muffins. I baked them at 350 degrees for about 15 minutes. I had enough batter for 12 muffins and put the extra in a loaf pan and have cut that up into bit sized squares. This could be a dessert or a breakfast!

I made this with 1/3 c veg. Oil and 1/3 c. Milk. Also subbed in 1/3 c. Light agave nectar for the sugar (mix this in with wet ingredients). If using mini choc. Chips I would recommend 1/2-3/4 cups as the chocolate gets overpowering. Baked at 350 degrees convection bake and they came out moist and perfect at 20 minutes! Yum!

Yum! Easy to make with ingredients on hand. I used 1/3 cup canola oil and 1/3 cup applesauce - instead of the 2/3 cup oil. Used 3/4 cup chocolate chips, which was plenty for our tastes! Also, turned the temp. down to 375 degrees and baked for 20 minutes. Used toothpick to check for doneness. Will make these again and again. Thanks!

Yummy! I used King Arthur white whole wheat flour, Hershey's Special Dark cocoa powder, and subbed canola oil for sunflower. The batter seemed a bit dense so I added a splash of almond milk. Baked at 375 for a total of about 23 min. I wanted to add a little something so after they cooled a bit I dipped the tops in a cream cheese/powdered sugar glaze and sprinkled with toasted coconut. The texture of the muffin was perfect. Will definitely make these again.

Extremely good! I used 1/2 oil and 1/2 milk instead of all oil and I used 1/2 white and 1/2 brown sugar. Also added 2 extra tablespoons of sugar! I baked them for 18 minutes,but at 350*,not the 425! They rose beautifully and were extremely moist! So glad I found this recipe! Thank you! And when I doubled it, I got 32 large muffins!

Easy and tasty recipe. I used 1/3 c canola oil and 1/3 c unsweetened applesauce. Used 3 medium bananas; next time I will add at least one more because I think the bananas were overpowered by the chocolate flavor. Batter was slightly thick so I added 2 Tbs milk to loosen it up. All in all --- a success!

I don’t typically change things in a recipe without trying it BUT I read some other reviews and decided to use their changes. I used brown sugar instead of white. Once I got everything mixed together it seemed a very dry so I added about 1/3 cup of milk. I baked at the normal temp for 15 minutes and they turned out perfect! Very moist and delicious!

I do not see how people were getting dry banana (reading some of the reviews) remember its 1 1/2 cups mashed banana, not 1 1/2 cup banana then mash, and use riper banana, nice soft bananas right before they turn brown inside, after the pealing have gone past all yellow. I used four large ripe bananas and mine came out great! I did bake it at only 400, I would even go down to 375 not the 425. They are fantastic though!
These tasted very nice! They came out exactly as shown in the photo. I baked it at a lower temp 350 F, for about 15 minutes. Came out perfectly cooked.
Very thick batter. I used chocolate milk to thin it out. It had great choc flavor but the banana flavor was lost. Texture was light and spongy.
Love these! I used: 1/2 Swerve 1/2 sugar 1/3 oil 1/3 applesauce Miniature chocolate chips (these distribute more evenly) A little More diabetic friendly
Delicious and great recipe. I used 4 ripe bananas in it. Mine could have been baked for slightly less than the maximum in the recipe.
425 seemed hot but followed the recipe. They were burning well before 15 minutes was up. After reading reviews seems like a lot of tweaks are needed. Won’t be attempting these again
Well... they’re OK. The rest of my family loved these! I made a double batch and 2 days ago and they’re already gone! Definitely make for kids!
These muffins tasted like flour. Expensive experiment!
Have made these numerous times. Much better at 400 for about 15-17 min. I added flax meal for a healthy shot and topped them with some raw sugar.
I made them with gluten free flour & they were very yummy!

These were very tasty! I was looking for a banana muffin recipe that didn’t include milk since I was out. I also didn’t use chocolate chips since I didn’t have any and still came out yummy and moist. I’m sure would taste even better with them!
